stimuli.title: In a certain coded language, each word has one unique code.
stimuli.body:
meadow feather planet = ni ka po
river mango feather = mu zu ka
planet winter river = sa mu po
winter meadow mango = sa zu ni
stimuli.solution: feather=ka, planet=po, meadow=ni, river=mu, mango=zu, winter=sa

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain S = X > Z ≥ P = T, decide which conclusions follow. I: Z ≥ T. II: S = T.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Exhaustive valid-order checking confirms: I is always true and II is not necessarily true.

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain R < P = S > V ≤ W, decide which conclusions follow. I: P ≥ S. II: S < W.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Exhaustive valid-order checking confirms: I is always true and II is not necessarily true.

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain Z = V < Q < U ≤ P, decide which conclusions follow. I: Z ≥ P. II: V < U.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Exhaustive valid-order checking confirms: I is not necessarily true and II is always true.

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain W ≥ P ≤ Q ≥ V ≥ T, decide which conclusions follow. I: Q ≥ T. II: P ≤ Q.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Exhaustive valid-order checking confirms: I is always true and II is always true.

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain W ≥ S = T < R = X, decide which conclusions follow. I: W ≥ S. II: S ≤ T.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Exhaustive valid-order checking confirms: I is always true and II is always true.

questions.stem: Statements: All bakers are artists. Some drivers are bakers. Conclusions: I. Some drivers are artists. II. Some artists are drivers. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: The existing C∩A members must lie in B, proving both conclusions.

questions.stem: Statements: No coders are dancers. All painters are dancers. Some painters are dancers. Conclusions: I. No coders are painters. II. Some painters are not coders. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: All C members belong to B, disjoint from A; some C are explicitly given.

questions.stem: Statements: Some dancers are runners. Some runners are singers. Conclusions: I. Some dancers are singers. II. All singers are dancers. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: The specified intersections do not force A and C to overlap or include one another.

questions.stem: Statements: Some artists are farmers. All farmers are teachers. Conclusions: I. Some artists are teachers. II. All artists are teachers. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Some A–B members must be C; not all A need be C.

questions.stem: Statements: No painters are workers. Some workers are coders. Conclusions: I. Some coders are not painters. II. No coders are painters. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: The B∩C members are outside A; other C members remain unrestricted.

questions.stem: Ritu walks 90 km north, then 72 km east, then 18 km south and finally 18 km west. What is her shortest distance from the starting point?
